paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across media outlets
model_annotation: This pie chart displays the distribution of articles across various media outlets, as referenced in a study on narrative media framing in political discourse. The chart contains approximately 18 slices, each representing a different media source. The largest slice belongs to Breitbart, shown in a brown/olive color and labeled at 14%, followed by "Other" in green at 13%. Drudge Report appears as a large pink/salmon-colored slice at 8%, and The Daily Caller is shown in a dark gray slice also at 8%. The Huffington Post is represented by a brown slice at 7%, NPR by a teal/dark cyan slice at 6%, and Vox by an orange slice also at 6%. The Guardian appears in a darker shade at 5%, and BBC is shown at approximately 4%. Several smaller slices, each labeled at 3%, represent RT, Daily Kos, National Review, Daily Mail, Red State, Fox News, CNN, PoliticusUSA, and Shareblue, displayed in various colors including purple, light blue, red, gray, and other distinguishing hues. Percentage labels are placed inside or near each slice, and category labels are positioned around the outside of the chart rather than in a separate legend. The slices appear to be arranged roughly in descending order of size moving clockwise from the top, with the smallest slices clustered together in the lower portion of the chart. No slices appear to be visually exploded or offset from the center.
